research_question: When the cardiac cycle is known, does REM-Net's continuous output carry better beat morphology than the five matched baselines' outputs under the same loso_v2 protocol?
no_training: Frozen test predictions only. Nothing is trained, tuned or selected; no model, checkpoint, threshold or lag is chosen from these numbers.

metric_definition.cycle: per window, the R-R interval whose midpoint is closest to the window centre, cut from GT R peaks (scripts/train_continuous_ecg_pilot._centre_cycle); windows with fewer than two R peaks or a cycle of 10 samples or fewer are skipped and counted
metric_definition.resampling: prediction and ground truth each linearly resampled to 200 samples over the same cycle
metric_definition.normalization: each resampled cycle min-max normalized to [0, 1], independently for prediction and ground truth (identical to shape200_pcc)
metric_definition.within_fold: mean over windows with a valid cycle (window-macro)
metric_definition.across_folds: fold-macro mean with population std over 11 test subjects
metric_definition.consistency_check: per-fold PCC must equal scripts/train_continuous_ecg_pilot.shape200_pcc on the same arrays

statistics: paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 11 fold-level values, REM-Net versus each baseline, plus the count of folds REM-Net wins; no multiplicity correction is applied and five comparisons are reported, so p-values are descriptive
reporting_rules: Tier 1 uses GT R peaks to define the cycle; it is a known-cycle morphology upper bound and must never be described as continuous ECG reconstruction.
These numbers come from models trained for the continuous task. They are not comparable to the old trained-for-Shape-200 figure (0.882), which is BLOCKED.
Report PCC with RMSE and MAE, never PCC alone.
follow_up: W1b, a Tier-1 trained rerun on loso_v2, is specified after this readout (docs/Q1_JOURNAL_MASTER_PLAN.md, W1).
